title: Frictionless action snapshots and client rehydration (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc sketches a low-friction pattern for capturing compact action snapshots during streaming responses and using them to rehydrate client SDK state for resume, offline replay, and resumable tool-choreography. The goal is a pragmatic API and SDK ergonomics surface that reduces developer glue code and failure modes for long-lived/partial sessions (mobile, flaky networks, rate-limited clients).

Problem statement (concise)
- Hosted streaming sessions frequently cross brittle boundaries: mobile disconnects, device sleep, client upgrades, and multi-device handoffs.
- Tool calls and structured outputs can be partially emitted; clients today must either (a) persist raw deltas and reapply logic, (b) re-run expensive model prompts, or (c) accept inconsistent UX.
- Existing resume approaches require heavy client bookkeeping (token offsets, schema diffs, tool idempotency checks).

User scenarios
- Mobile note-taking app: user generates a structured action (TODO items + attachments) over a 3–4 minute stream; phone goes offline then comes back on a different device. App expects to continue from last reliable action and finish tool calls only once.
- Customer support agent: long chat with incremental tool lookups (KB retrievals, DB writes). Agent wants to pause, examine intermediate tool results, and resume without losing partial work or double-invoking side effects.
- Background batch worker: resumes partial streaming outputs for audit/eval with minimal re-computation.

Goals
- Provide a compact, verifiable snapshot format representing the minimal resume state required by the server and SDK to continue a session deterministically.
- Make snapshots cheap/network-friendly and opt-in per session.
- Define clear semantics for tool-call side effects to avoid double-execution on resume (idempotency, tombstones, transactional handles).
- Provide an SDK helper that handles snapshot lifecycle, persistence strategy, and reconciling incremental server deltas on resume.

Non-goals
- This is not a general-purpose CRDT sync system for arbitrarily concurrent edits.
- We do not implement a full distributed consensus for tool-call side effects; we provide primitives to minimize and reason about double-execution risk.

High-level approach
1) Streamed response contains periodic snapshot frames (compact JSON blobs) that capture: last-processed model token offset, last-completed tool call ids + lightweight summaries, and a small set of named variables (session-scoped KV) required to rehydrate program state.
2) Snapshots are signed by the service (HMAC) to allow clients to present them on resume and for the server to detect tampering/old snapshots. Signature keys rotate per-deployment but are validated by the control plane.
3) On resume, client sends: session_id, snapshot_blob, and optionally a replay-mode flag (continue | inspect-only | replay). Server validates snapshot and returns a streaming delta that picks up from the exact token boundary.

Snapshot shape (proposal)
- snapshot_version: string (v1)
- token_cursor: string (opaque token offset)
- tool_state: list of {tool_id, invocation_id, status, result_summary_hash}
- small_vars: list of {name, value} (for short program state like buffers, user preferences)
- client_checkpoint_meta: {client_sdk_version, platform, persisted_at}
- server_signature: string (base64)
(We keep everything flat and small; no embedded large outputs.)

Tool-call semantics and anti-duplication strategy
- Each tool call emitted in-stream must carry an invocation_id (UUID) generated by the server or client (configurable). The server preserves a compact idempotency map keyed by invocation_id for a TTL (e.g., 7 days) per-customer.
- Snapshots include the last-known status for each invocation_id (pending | completed | cancelled) and a result_summary_hash when available. On resume, server uses invocation_id + client opt-in policy to decide whether to re-run or return cached result.
- For non-idempotent side effects (writes), the SDK offers two modes: optimistic (client assumes server will not re-run) or transactional (client requests a server-side transactional handle that guarantees single execution). Transactional handles may require enterprise plan due to resource/tracking cost.

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing)
- SDK exposes a SessionSnapshot object with methods:
  - capture_periodic(interval_ms) -> registers automatic snapshotting to local persistence
  - persist(path_hint) -> returns snapshot_blob for custom persistence
  - resume(session_id, snapshot_blob, mode) -> rehydrates and returns a streaming iterator
  - on_tool_invocation(invocation_meta) -> hooks to register client-local side-effects
- Default behavior: SDK will capture snapshots every N bytes of streamed structured output or on tool-call completion. SDK persists to a pluggable store (local storage for web, SQLite for mobile, file for node).

Storage and bandwidth considerations
- Snapshots are intentionally limited to a few KB. Large tool results must live in the server storage and be referenced via opaque handles included in the snapshot (result_summary_hash + small url). This avoids snapshot bloat.
- SDK will gzip snapshots in transit. Server validates decompressed size and rejects > 16KB (configurable guardrail).

Resume handshake (example flow)
1) Client reconnects and calls /sessions/{id}/resume with Authorization + snapshot_blob + mode.
2) Server verifies signature and snapshot freshness; if stale, returns HTTP 409 with guidance (recompute from last stable checkpoint) and a small delta token.
3) If valid, server returns a small ACK frame then starts streaming from token_cursor.
4) For pending tool invocations, server emits either cached results or an explicit re-invocation event depending on policy. Each re-invocation event includes invocation_id and a decision flag (replay or skip).

Failure modes and mitigations
- Missing snapshot: fall back to conservative restart (re-run prompts) and surface to client that some side effects may duplicate. SDK warns user if transactional handles not used.
- Signature mismatch: client prompts for force-resume via manual confirmation, or falls back to session restart.
- Stale invocation_id map: server may not have record of an invocation_id anymore; SDK should surface to user and optionally show the original intent to confirm re-execution.

Migration and compatibility
- v1 snapshot parser will be tolerant: unknown fields are ignored. We will version snapshots to allow future richer state.
- Older SDKs that don't understand snapshots will continue to function (server will not require snapshots) but will get degraded resume UX.

Privacy and security
- Snapshots may contain small user-provided strings (short prompt fragments). We will document that snapshots should not contain PII. Customers may opt-out of snapshotting for sensitive workloads.
- Snapshots are encrypted at rest in customer storage by SDK adapters and HMAC-signed in transit.

Open questions (short list)
- TTL for server-side invocation idempotency map: 3 days vs 7 days vs 30 days? Tradeoff: storage cost vs safety.
- Transactional handles: what resource accounting and billing model? (enterprise add-on?)
- Snapshot frequency default: every 5s, every 2KB, or every tool-call event?
- How to offer a first-class debug UI in Console to inspect snapshots and partial sessions?

Implementation plan (phased)
Phase 0 (experiment, 2 sprints)
- Implement prototype snapshot shape + server-side validate code + minimal SDK helpers (node + web).
- Integrate with streaming test harness and run 20 internal playbacks.
Phase 1 (beta, 4 sprints)
- Add persistent invocation idempotency map with configurable TTL, transactional handle MVP, mobile SDK adapters.
- Console: session inspector surfaces snapshots and tool invocation history.
Phase 2 (GA)
- Harden security (key rotation), enterprise transactional SLAs, telemetry + evals for double-exec incidence.

Telemetry & success metrics
- Fraction of resumed sessions that successfully continue without re-prompting (target > 90% within 3 months of beta)
- Duplicate side-effect rate (target < 0.5% for idempotent flows)
- Average snapshot size and frequency (track for bandwidth billing)

Notes & TODOs (brainstorm-y)
- Consider offering a server-side compact dump endpoint for offline audit (session_id -> final snapshot) for compliance teams.
- Investigate using deterministic token cursors that are independent of internal tokenization changes.
- UX: expose a simple toggle in Console per-API-key to enable snapshotting and TTL policy.

Appendix: example snapshot blob (v1)
{"snapshot_version": "v1", "token_cursor": "tkn_0000c3f9", "tool_state": ["tool_id:kb_search|invocation_id:123e4567|status:completed|hash:ab12cd"], "small_vars": ["title:Meeting notes|progress:0.6"], "client_checkpoint_meta": "sdk:node-0.21|platform:web|persisted_at:2025-01-10T12:03:00Z", "server_signature": "base64sig..."}

Next steps (for this draft)
- Product/Eng sync (this week): validate feasibility of idempotency map cost estimate. (Ethan)
- UX spike: Console inspector mockups and sample developer docs for SDK persistence patterns. (Sana)
- Wire up simple end-to-end prototype with mobile SDK (Liam)

-- end of draft --
